newsitem.title: USA: Counties create Internet welfare information site.
newsitem.headline: Counties create Internet welfare information site.

text.p: The National Association of Counties said on Wednesday it had opened an Internet welfare reform clearinghouse site to allow local officials to track the progress of welfare reform nationally.

Association president Michael Hightower said that "With the National Internet Clearninghouse (NICH), we have created a system that will give counties the radar to see what welfare programs are working all over the country."

The association said it hoped the Internet site would help alleviate some of the chaos associated with implementing the new national welfare reform law by giving local officials timely information on its impact at the local levels.
It said the site -- http://www.naco.org/nich -- would give local officials access to specific county, region and state welfare reform information within minutes.

Hightower, who is a Fulton County, Ga., commissioner, told a news conference that "If you want to find out how many people in any county of the country are getting welfare assistance, NICH will help you find the number."
The association said many county officials are in need of such a database because they expect to be held responsible for many services not adequately covered by the states.
